lines: A six-row, sixteen-step gate sequencer with a built-in clock, a timing offset for each row, a probability for each step, and eleven genre pattern generators on the menu
Turns that step on for its row; a right-click on it opens a menu setting how often that step fires
Moves that row's triggers off the beat in clock ticks, up to fifteen of the sixteen ticks that make a step; anticlockwise fires early and clockwise fires late
Sets how many of the sixteen steps are played before the pattern starts over, snapping to whole steps; at 0 the sequencer stops and the row outputs hold what they last had
Sets the internal clock rate, from 80ms a tick at the anticlockwise end of its travel to 3ms at the clockwise end; sixteen ticks make one step
Chooses between Cont, where a row's output stays high for the whole of an active step, and Trig, where it sends a 1ms pulse; the module comes up on Trig
Generates a fresh pattern from the genre picked on the menu, and sets every step's probability back to 100%
Shifts that row one step earlier, wrapping the first step round to the end, and carries each step's probability with it
Shifts that row one step later, wrapping the last step round to the front, and carries each step's probability with it
The external clock; while a cable is patched here the internal clock is not used, and the module counts sixteen pulses to one of its steps
Sends the sequencer back to the first step on any change away from 0V; clock pulses in the millisecond after it are ignored
Generates a fresh pattern from the genre picked on the menu on each rise away from 0V, and sets every step's probability back to 100%
10V while the row marked KICK fires and 0V otherwise; the genre generators write their kick part into that row
10V while the row marked SNARE fires and 0V otherwise; the genre generators write their snare part into that row
10V while the row marked HH CL fires and 0V otherwise; the genre generators write their closed hi-hat part into that row
10V while the row marked HH OP fires and 0V otherwise; the genre generators write their open hi-hat part into that row
10V while the row marked PERC 1 fires and 0V otherwise; the genre generators write their first percussion part into that row
10V while the row marked PERC 2 fires and 0V otherwise; the genre generators write their second percussion part into that row
The internal clock as a 1ms pulse at 10V; while a cable is in the external clock input this jack passes that clock through instead
Note — A step set to 0% on the probability menu fires every time rather than never, because the code treats a probability of zero as a deterministic step. The maker's readme says 0% never triggers.
Note — Step probabilities and the chosen genre are not saved with the patch and come back at their defaults when it is reloaded; the gate switches themselves are saved, being ordinary parameters.
Note — A newly placed module has every step's probability at 0, which is the fires-every-time case.
Note — The lamp inside a gate switch is blanked for any step whose probability is below 100%, so on a fresh module none of them lights until Random is pressed or the probabilities are cleared.
Note — The row of lamps under the grid shows which step the sequencer has reached.
Note — The maker's readme specifies sixty-four clock pulses per quarter note, which is 128Hz at 120 BPM; sixteen of those pulses make one step of the grid.
Menu — Randomize all gates — sets all ninety-six gate switches on or off at random
Menu — Randomize Gates for row 1 — sets the sixteen gate switches of that row on or off at random, with one such item per row
Menu — Generate by genre: House, Techno, Trap, Drum & Bass, Minimal, Afro, Electro, Ambient, Glitch, Braindance, Markovian — fills the grid from that genre's rules and sets what Random makes
Menu — Clear all probabilities — sets every step's probability to 100%
Menu — Step probability: 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% — on a gate switch's own right-click menu, sets how often that step fires

InteractiveRhythmComposer.notes: Source read at commit 903f513. Every recent commit says version 2.0.0, so the installed files settled it: plugin.json and both panel SVGs match commits 903f513, 4182b18, 6b77cfe, a559ac6 and cc650ea, and the installed binary calls the ShiftArrowButtonLeft and ShiftArrowButtonRight constructors six times each, which rules out the three commits where only the first row used those widgets. That leaves 903f513 and 4182b18, whose James.cpp is identical. Three faults. First, James.cpp:731 tests if (prob <= 0.f || random::uniform() < prob), so the 0% choice on the step probability menu makes the step fire every time; the readme says 0% never triggers. Second, there is no dataToJson or dataFromJson anywhere in the module, so the 96 step probabilities and the selected genre are lost when a patch is saved. Third, gateProbabilities is default-initialised to zero at James.cpp:595, so a fresh module is in that 0% state throughout, and ProbableGateSwitch::draw paints a dark circle over the lamp of every switch whose probability is below 1, which blanks the whole grid's lamps until Random or Clear all probabilities has been used. The six rush knobs are configured with the minimum above the maximum, 15 down to -15, and the value is negated again at James.cpp:606, so the anticlockwise end is the early offset. The maker named the six gate outputs Row 1 gate to Row 6 gate; the panel prints KICK, SNARE, HH CL, HH OP, PERC 1 and PERC 2, and the lines follow the panel.
